# Paris Apartment Rental Checklist for 2026-09-01

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

A lease in Paris usually goes smoothly when you verify the guarantor terms, security deposit limits, inventory process, and notice rules before signing.
I’m assuming this is a standard unfurnished or furnished private rental in Paris, not social housing or a short-term tourist rental.

## What to Review Before You Sign

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

- **Guarantor requirement**
  - Ask whether the landlord wants a **physical person guarantor** or a **Visale**-type guarantee.
  - Confirm exactly what documents the guarantor must provide and whether one guarantor is enough.
  - Make sure the guarantor obligation is limited to the lease term and clearly written.

- **Security deposit**
  - Check the deposit amount against the lease type:
    - **Unfurnished:** usually up to **1 month of rent excluding charges**
    - **Furnished:** usually up to **2 months of rent excluding charges**
  - Confirm what is included in “charges” and how the deposit will be returned.

- **Inventory report / entry inspection**
  - The **état des lieux d’entrée** should be done carefully on move-in day.
  - Every room, appliance, wall, floor, and meter reading should be recorded.
  - Add photos and written notes for any scratches, stains, cracks, or missing items.

- **Notice period**
  - Confirm your notice period for ending the lease.
  - In Paris, tenant notice is often **1 month** in many cases, especially for furnished rentals and in many urban situations, but the lease wording must be checked.
  - Make sure the contract does not add an unfair notice obligation.

- **Lease essentials**
  - Rent amount, charges, payment date, and rent review clause
  - Lease start date: **2026-09-01**
  - Who pays for minor repairs, maintenance, and utilities
  - Whether the property is furnished and what inventory is included
  - Subletting rules, visitor rules, and renewal conditions

## Tenant Document Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

Prepare these documents in a clean PDF set:

- **Identity**
  - Passport or national ID
  - Residence permit if applicable

- **Proof of income**
  - Recent payslips
  - Employment contract or employer letter
  - Last tax return or tax notice if available
  - Bank statements if requested

- **Housing history**
  - Previous landlord reference
  - Current proof of address
  - Proof of current rent payment if relevant

- **Guarantor file**
  - Guarantor ID
  - Proof of address
  - Proof of income
  - Employment proof
  - Latest tax notice or equivalent income proof
  - Signed guarantor commitment if required

- **Rental application extras**
  - Student certificate if applicable
  - Work contract start date if you are relocating
  - A short cover note introducing your profile

## Common Problems to Avoid

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

- Signing before the **inventory report** is completed
- Paying a deposit without a written lease and receipt
- Accepting vague guarantor language with no scope or end date
- Missing rent-charges split, which can create disputes later
- Assuming the notice period is the same for every lease type
- Forgetting to keep copies of every signed page and attachment

## French Email to Clarify the Guarantor Request

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/envelope.svg

**Objet :** Demande de précisions concernant la caution solidaire

Bonjour [Nom du propriétaire / de l’agence],

Merci pour votre retour concernant la location du logement à partir du **1er septembre 2026**.

Avant de finaliser le dossier, pourriez-vous me préciser les conditions exactes liées à la demande de garant ?
Je souhaiterais notamment savoir :

- si vous demandez une **caution solidaire d’une personne physique** ou un autre dispositif, comme **Visale** ;
- quels documents doivent être fournis par le garant ;
- si un seul garant suffit ;
- et si cette garantie couvre toute la durée du bail.

Je veux m’assurer que le dossier est complet et conforme avant la signature.

Merci d’avance pour votre aide.

Cordialement,
[Votre prénom et nom]
